access_surface: Linux notebook or local environment layered on top of MotionGPT tooling
prompt_guidance: Only target explicit combat gaps that manual sources could not cover.
Keep prompts short and clip-specific so pilot results are easy to evaluate.
Focus on baseline timing, contact pose, and readability over variety.
provenance_notes: Mark the run as pilot-only in provenance.
Record clip intent, estimated length, seed, and any retargeting notes.
Capture the exact reason manual animation sources were insufficient.
review_checklist: Clip solves a concrete combat gap instead of creating a speculative library.
Timing and pose readability are good enough for first-fight combat proof.
Animation export remains isolated until reviewed and accepted.
setup_steps: Treat AnimationGPT as a pilot stack because the public repo is a thin layer over MotionGPT, not a polished asset tool.
Use the documented Python 3.10 and MotionGPT-based environment before trying to run the demo pipeline.
Plan for a conversion step from raw motion outputs into a reviewable animation format before Blender cleanup or retargeting.
progression_steps: Only open this lane after Mixamo or other manual sources leave a specific combat gap.
Generate one clip intention at a time, convert it, retarget it, and test it in a minimal combat slice immediately.
If cleanup or retarget cost is too high, stop the pilot and go back to manual animation sourcing.
runbook: Use only when Mixamo/manual clips leave a clear gameplay gap.
Review in a minimal combat slice before adding more generated animation work.
Do not treat pilot results as a finished shared animation baseline without review.
